intro_html: Turns the four clicks and three screens that follow every routine sales order — validate the delivery, create the invoice, post it — into a single Confirm, for the warehouses where none of that needs a human decision.

features.title: Ship on confirm
features.desc: Validates the delivery in full the moment the order is confirmed — all lines, full quantity, no backorder.

features.title: Invoice on confirm
features.desc: Runs exactly what the manual Create Invoice button runs, so every product keeps its own invoicing policy.

features.title: Posted, not draft
features.desc: The invoice this run just created goes straight to Posted — nothing waits in a draft queue for someone to notice.

features.title: Set per warehouse
features.desc: Automate the warehouse that ships routine orders and leave the project warehouse fully manual. Three independent switches.

features.title: All-or-nothing
features.desc: Every step runs in one transaction. If anything fails, the order stays a quotation — no stray delivery, no orphan invoice.

features.title: A message, not a traceback
features.desc: A failure names the stage that broke and the reason in plain words, so the person confirming the order knows what to fix.

features.title: Nothing to invoice is fine
features.desc: When there is genuinely nothing invoiceable yet, that step is skipped, noted in the chatter, and the order confirms normally.

features.title: Nothing new to learn
features.desc: Three checkboxes on the warehouse form. No new menu, no new screen, no new model — the Confirm button your team already uses does the rest.

limitations: No partial shipping — automatic delivery is all-or-nothing for the whole order.
No stock availability check — negative stock is intended behaviour on automatic warehouses.
Lot- and serial-tracked products are out of scope: a required lot is a real failure, not a silent skip.
No per-order override and no exceptions list — the switches are per warehouse only.
Invoices are posted, never emailed to the customer.
A rolled-back order shows no trace of the attempt; the audit trail is developer-facing only.
Nothing is retried — a failed confirmation must be confirmed again by hand once the cause is fixed.
